dataset.description:
Cancer remains a global health problem, due to its mechanisms of resistance that hinder the development of effective treatment. The intratumoral expression of immunomodulatory genes, encompassing cytokines, chemokines, co-stimulatory molecules, and antibodies for induction of an anti-tumor immune response represents a promising therapeutic strategy. The main challenges in such solid tumor treatment include targeting, distribution, and adequate expression of therapeutic genes in the tumor tissue. Virus vectors have shown remarkable efficiency as naturally evolved systems for gene transfer. However, anti-vector immunity and unspecific targeting remain a problem. In this study, we propose delivering alphaviral RNA replicon with advanced liposomes targeting cancer-specific molecules (folate, HER2). Furthermore, we expect that employing a cellular membrane fusion phenomenon through the formation of syncytia would allow efficient RNA replicon distribution within the tumor. The HTLV1 hyperfusogenic env gene variant will be expressed by the alphaviral RNA replicon to ensure an efficient spread and induction of immunogenic cell death in 2D and 3D cancer cell models. In summary, this project will generate a novel approach to deliver alphaviral RNA replicon to cancer cells as a potential immunotherapy vector.
Keywords: alphaviral RNA, cancer immunotherapy, syncytium-mediated distribution, liposomal delivery

distribution.title:
The purpose of data collection and generation in this project is to design, validate, and evaluate a targeted alphaviral RNA replicon (repRNA) delivery platform for cancer gene therapy, including liposome-mediated targeting and syncytium-mediated intratumoral dissemination in 2D and 3D cancer cell models. The data will directly support the project objectives by (i) confirming construction and functional expression of repRNA vectors encoding HTLV1 env and immunomodulatory genes, (ii) characterizing physicochemical properties, targeting specificity, and stability of newly synthesized lipid nanoparticles, and (iii) assessing cytopathic effects, syncytia formation, macrophage activation, phagocytosis, and cytokine responses in 3D spheroid co-culture systems. The data will originate primarily from experimental laboratory work conducted within the project (molecular cloning, in vitro RNA synthesis, nanoparticle synthesis and characterization, microscopy, flow cytometry, ELISA/Luminex assays, gene expression analysis, and functional cell-based assays), with secondary datasets generated through statistical processing, image analysis, and quantitative data normalization.
Primary data:
• Experimental laboratory data (molecular biology, cell biology, gene editing validation)
• Flow cytometry data
• Microscopy and imaging data (2D, 3D, in vivo imaging)
• Functional assay data (migration, cytotoxicity, phagocytosis, cytokine quantification)
Secondary data:
• Processed and normalized quantitative datasets
• Statistical analysis outputs
• Annotated image analysis results

dmp.description: This Data Management Plan (DMP) outlines the strategy for managing research data generated within the project “Targeted delivery and syncytium-mediated distribution of alphaviral RNA replicon in 3D cancer cell model” The project aims to develop an innovative alphaviral RNA replicon (repRNA) platform for targeted cancer gene therapy, combining cancer-specific liposomal nanocarriers with a fusogenic HTLV1 env gene to enhance intratumoral distribution and immunogenic cell death in 2D and 3D cancer models. The scope of the DMP covers the full data lifecycle, including generation, documentation, storage, quality control, protection, sharing, and long-term preservation of molecular biology data, nanoparticle characterization results, imaging datasets, functional assay outputs, and macrophage phenotyping analyses. The objective of the Plan is to ensure that all experimental and analytical data are managed in a secure, structured, and reproducible manner, in compliance with FAIR principles and institutional, ethical, and funding requirements, while enabling appropriate dissemination and future reuse of non-sensitive datasets.
dmp.title: Targeted delivery and syncytium-mediated distribution of alphaviral RNA replicon in 3D cancer cell model
